record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For fully decentralized learning under non-IID client data, how can one understand convergence and design model-averaging policies that achieve the fastest convergence, especially when clients perform several local update steps before communication?

evidence.quote: understanding the convergence under non-IID data distributions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a fully decentralized optimization problem of the form

  minimize  F(x) = (1/n) Σ_{i=1}^n F_i(x),    F_i(x) = E_{ξ∼D_i}[ f(x; ξ) ],

where n clients (nodes) are arranged on a connected communication graph G=(V,E) and the local data distributions D_1,…,D_n are heterogeneous (non-IID), so that the local gradients ∇F_i may differ substantially from the global gradient ∇F. Communication is restricted to neighbors in G and is encoded by a sequence of symmetric doubly-stochastic mixing matrices {W_t} ⊂ R^{n×n} supported on G.

Each client i maintains a local model x_i^{(t)} ∈ R^d. In each communication round, every client performs H ≥ 1 local stochastic gradient steps,

  y_i^{(t,0)} = x_i^{(t)},
  y_i^{(t,h+1)} = y_i^{(t,h)} − η ∇f(y_i^{(t,h)}; ξ_i^{(t,h)}),  h = 0,…,H−1,

and then performs a gossip averaging step using the mixing matrix W_t:

  x_i^{(t+1)} = Σ_{j=1}^n (W_t)_{ij} · y_j^{(t,H)}.

Under standard assumptions on f (L-smoothness, possibly (non)convexity, bounded stochastic gradient variance σ^2, and a bounded heterogeneity measure such as (1/n)Σ_i ‖∇F_i(x) − ∇F(x)‖^2 ≤ ζ^2), address the following:

(a) Derive convergence guarantees (rates as functions of n, H, η, σ^2, ζ^2, and the spectral properties of the mixing matrices, such as the second-largest singular value ρ = ‖W − (1/n)11^T‖) that quantify how non-IID data and the number H of local steps affect the convergence of the iterates {x_i^{(t)}} toward a stationary point or minimizer of F.

(b) Determine model-averaging policies — i.e., choices of the (possibly time-varying) mixing matrices W_t supported on G, the local step count H, and the step size η — that achieve the fastest possible convergence rate in this setting, and identify lower bounds matching these rates so as to characterize the optimal averaging policy for decentralized learning with multiple local updates under client data heterogeneity.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on understanding decentralized SGD convergence under non-IID data with local steps. Koloskova et al. (ICML 2020) gave a unified convergence theory for decentralized SGD with changing topology and local updates, and subsequent works (e.g., gradient-tracking variants, Huang et al. 2022, momentum-based unified frameworks 2024) have improved dependence on heterogeneity. However, fully characterizing optimal time-varying mixing policies and matching lower bounds, especially with many local steps under heterogeneity, remains an active area without a definitive closed answer.

status_evidence.title: A Unified Theory of Decentralized SGD with Changing Topology and Local Updates
status_evidence.snippet: Unified convergence analysis covering decentralized SGD methods with local updates and gossip on adaptive topologies; interpolates between iid and heterogeneous data.
status_evidence.claim: Partial convergence theory exists for decentralized SGD under non-IID data with local steps.

status_evidence.title: Tackling Data Heterogeneity: A New Unified Framework for Decentralized SGD
status_evidence.snippet: New unified framework analyzing decentralized SGD under data heterogeneity using gradient tracking-like techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works refine heterogeneity dependence but optimal mixing-policy design remains open.

status_evidence.title: A unified momentum-based paradigm of decentralized SGD for non-convex models and heterogeneous data
status_evidence.snippet: Momentum-based decentralized SGD framework for non-convex heterogeneous setting.
status_evidence.claim: Research is ongoing into optimal decentralized averaging under heterogeneity.
